newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks reduce gains at the close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks reduce gains at the close.

text.p: French shares closed higher on Monday but a last-minute bout of profit-taking eroded the early gains booked in a rebound to Friday's 2.26 percent slide on remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 15.12 points or 0.67 percent at 2,255.84, while the CAC-40 futures contract rose to 2,259 from 2,239 on Friday's close.
The CAC-index hit a day high of 2,264.13 and a low of 2,250.29. The December future hit resistance at 2,270.
Volume was 4.8 billion francs, of which 3.2 billion in CAC-40 shares.
The market opened with a jump after it realised that the Wall Street slide was less dramatic than it appeared on Friday afternoon and because the dollar and the Tokyo stock market held firm.

During the trading day, shares ran out of steam and were marking time ahead of the Wall Street opening. After the New York market's higher start, French shares took off again only to fall victim to profit-taking in the last half hour.
Dealers said market sentiment remained fragile and investors would remain sidelined to await the U.S. producer price index on Wednesday and consumer price index on Thursday.
The European Union summit in Dublin on monetary union, starting on Friday but preceded by a finance ministers' meeting on Thursday, is also keeping investors on their toes.

On Thursday, president Jacques Chirac will address the nation in a televised interview but he is not expected to make sweeping announcements. Another key date is December 17 when Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet will host a news conference on monetary policy after a bank council meeting. That same day the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee will meet.
"It's a nice recovery," a dealer said about today's rise. But, he warned, "We could still hit another air pocket."

At the fringes of a G-10 central banker's meeting in Basle, Switzerland, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said Friday's market reaction to Greenspan's comment that the share market was driven by "irrational exuberance" was overdone.
In Singapore, IMF managing director Michel Camdessus said however that Greenspan was right.

* Club Mediterannee was the biggest riser, ending 8.80 percent higher at 344.90 on a speculative rise after key shareholders ended a 1990 pact, making the company more vulnerable to a takeover. Paribas Capital Markets, SGE Delahaye and Dupont-Denant issued "buy" recommendations.

* Lagardere added 5.63 percent to 150 francs. Dealers said the share was supported by comments by Prime Minister Alain Juppe in the Financial Times. Juppe reiterated in the interview that the state could split Thomson SA and sell the 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF separately from loss-making Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
"We get the impression that the government wants Lagardere to get Thomson-CSF," an analyst said.
Thomson-CSF gained 1.77 percent to 167.00 francs.
* Skis Rossignol fell 2.07 percent to 137 francs after lower first-half results and a full-year profit warning.

* UAP, most actively traded share and up 1.74 percent at 134.40 francs, left the CAC-40 today but there is no replacement pending the outcome of its merger with AXA, up 1.6 percent. Sodexho, BIC and Usinor-Sacilor seen as candidates to take its place.
Their stay in the index could be short-lived as France Telecom is set to enter in spring after its partial privatisation.
* Eurotunnel, up 3.62 percent at 7.15 francs, also actively traded after reporting higher year-on-year November traffic and confirming December 10 restart of shuttle service.
* Renault among biggest fallers with 2.2 percent loss to 114.30 in prolonged slide on disappointing car sales.
* Brokerage house Wargny lowered its recommendation on Cap Gemini, up 1.36 percent to 246 francs, to hold from buy after concluding that it was trading at the right price, portfolio managers said.

* After closing, the Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) state bank said it had received 90.50 percent of Credit Foncier de France share in its buy-out bid on the state's behalf of the troubled property lender.
-- Marcel Michelson, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
